newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: POLITICIANS WON'T COMMIT ON NATIONAL'S NATIVE TITLE DEMAND
The Aboriginal Affairs Minister, John Herron, says it's too early to respond to the National Party president's demand that native title on pastoral leases be extinguished.
Senator Herron says the government's still consulting on native title.
The Nationals' President, Don McDonald, wants federal parliament to legislate to validate all leases.
In Charleville today, party leader Tim Fischer is playing down any split in the coalition over Native Title.
He says the Prime Minister is trying to complete the task urgently and there are no soft options.
The Kimberley Land Council has described the call as unfortunate.
Land Council executive director, Peter Yu, says there's always been pressure on the Prime Minister to extinguish native title.
Mr Yu says that during talks yesterday John Howard guaranteed that no position on native title had yet been developed.
NEW TECHNOLOGY MAY REPROCESS NUCLEAR WASTE IN AUSTRALIA
The federal government may use an Australian-developed method of reprocessing nuclear waste when storage space runs out next year.

Science and Technology Minister Peter McGauran says the Synrock method is one option under consideration for when the key storage site at Lucas Heights, in Sydney's south, reaches capacity at the end of 1998.
Mr McGauran says the government still has a year to find the best way to dispose of the spent radioactive rods.
Last year more than 100 radioactive rods from the National Science and Technology Organisation were shipped to a processor in Scotland.
MELBOURNE CHOKES AS WELL AS SWEATS
On top of four days of hot weather, Victoria's Environmental Protection Agency has declared a smog alert in Melbourne today.
A thick haze over the city has joined the 37 degree temperatures in which one man has died and there have been public warnings that heatstroke can be fatal.
But the EPA says the smog shouldn't pose a health risk at this stage because ozone levels are not high.
However, people with respiratory complaints should carry their medication with them, avoid exercise and take all of the standard precautions.
RAFTER WINS IN FOUR-HOUR MATCH
Australia leads one nil in the Davis Cup against France, after Patrick Rafter fought back from being down two sets to love to win the opening tie against Cedric Pioline.
After losing the first two sets 3-6, 6-7, Rafter went on to take the next three 6-4, 7-5, 6-4 in a match lasting just under four-and-a-half hours.
PILBARA FLOOD WATERS TO PEAK AGAIN
Emergency crews remain on standby in the west Pilbara as floodwaters from the swollen Ashburton River continue downstream.
Waters are expected to peak again late this afternoon at the plains near Onslow, about 80 kilometres west of the North West Highway.
State emergency workers say while Onslow itself is in no danger, two homesteads on the plain may be evacuated.
Overnight floodwaters peaked at 18-point-two metres at the Nanutarra settlement, higher than when Cyclone Bobby hit two years ago.
Local station owner Evan Pensini, who flew over the area this morning, says its the worst flood he's ever seen.
He believes it will take at least a few days for the water to clear.
Meanwhile, the State Emergency Service says the North West Coastal Highway will remain closed to all traffic between Minilya and Onslow.
Road users have been asked to delay their journeys and avoid the Ashburton River area until further notice.
MICHAEL LONG LEADS SA GOLF OPEN
Golfer Michael Long still leads the South Australian Open by two shots.
Long returned a six-under 66 today, to take the early second round lead.
American Tom Lehman, with three birdies in his outward nine, is challenging strongly, and are with Neil Kerry of New South Wales and Shane Tait of Queensland also at seven under par.
Craig Parry is five under, and Wayne Grady and Brett Ogle four under par.
Canadian Rick Gibson has fired a course record of seven-under-par 65 - to be also four-under after two rounds.
